what: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
text: Shows column types one data frames side--side, classifies column whether datasets row-bound . Useful diagnosing type mismatches join binding lazer::read_files().

title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
code: view_types(..., diff = FALSE, focus = NULL)

title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
text: ... Data frames compare (unquoted), single named list data frames, default output lazer::read_files(). list can also spliced !!!. Names inferred expressions passed, taken list. diff Logical. TRUE, columns status "conflict" shown, frames bind produce empty result. see every difference, filter status != "ok" instead. Default: FALSE. focus named character vector expected types, e.g. c(cvr = "chr", year = "int"). supplied, named columns shown, datasets type match (absent column counts mismatch). Returns empty tibble (0 rows) types match, can used checkpoints. Takes precedence diff.

title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
text: tibble column column, status column (see Details) one column per input dataset showing abbreviated type string ("int", "dbl", "chr", "fct", "date", "dttm", ...). NA means column absent dataset.

title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
text: type string alone say whether two data frames can stacked: int dbl bind without trouble, column entirely NA (readr reads empty column lgl). column absent one dataset obstacle either, since dplyr::bind_rows() fills NA. real conflict chr vs dbl makes bind fail, forces lazer::read_files() fall back character. status column therefore asks question function called : bind? "ok": present everywhere type. "coercible": present everywhere, types differ bind without loss structure (int + dbl, fct + chr, date + dttm, -NA lgl anything). "missing": absent least one dataset, conflict among rest. Typically rename dropped column upstream. "conflict": types combined. Compatibility tested binding zero-row slices column dplyr::bind_rows(), classification follows rules read_files(= "bind").

title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
code: df1 <- data.frame(x = 1L,  y = "a", z = NA) df2 <- data.frame(x = 1.0, y = 2,   z = "b")  view_types(df1, df2) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   column status    df1   df2   #>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> <chr> #> 1 x      coercible int   dbl   #> 2 y      conflict  chr   dbl   #> 3 z      coercible lgl   chr   view_types(df1, df2, diff = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   column status   df1   df2   #>   <chr>  <chr>    <chr> <chr> #> 1 y      conflict chr   dbl   view_types(df1, df2, focus = c(x = "int", y = "chr")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   column status    df2   #>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> #> 1 x      coercible dbl   #> 2 y      conflict  dbl    # A named list of data frames, e.g. from read_files(): view_types(list(a = df1, b = df2)) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   column status    a     b     #>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> <chr> #> 1 x      coercible int   dbl   #> 2 y      conflict  chr   dbl   #> 3 z      coercible lgl   chr
